answer: Coordination Ridge Pricing. Each agent's influence on shared decisions is capped by the entropy of its interaction history, measured as a ridge over its distinct counterparties; identities that act in lockstep share one budget. To enlarge that budget, an attacker must sustain diverse, non-repeating exchanges across an atlas of independent partners, and each fake identity pays its own verification and bandwidth cost, making a prism of split accounts strictly more expensive than one honest agent.
